thread:
acme-sre: Hey, we're seeing streaming responses from our Redwood Private deployment stall. Client gets nothing for ~30s, then a big chunk of tokens arrives all at once. Repro is consistent from our VPC through our NAT/egress GW.

maria_support: Sorry about that — can you confirm this only happens over your VPC/private deployment and not when you hit hosted API?

acme-sre: Correct — hosted API works fine. Only our VPC endpoint (private) shows the bursty behaviour. Happens with both chat and raw streaming generate endpoints.

jamal: Do you have any edge proxies or WAFs in the path? Middleboxes often buffer websocket frames when they see idle periods.

acme-sre: We have a managed firewall and an NGFW in front of the NAT gateway. We suspect there's some idle timeout. Any tests we can run to prove buffering vs idle-close?

sre_jen: Two quick checks: 1) run wscat and keep it open, send small messages every 10s to see if data flows continuously; 2) capture tcpdump on client side for a session showing the silence and then burst. If you see TCP window staying open and no FIN/RST, it's likely buffering, not close.

acme-sre: Attaching excerpt from tcpdump (sanitized).

acme-sre: ```
14:10:01.123 IP client > redwood: Flags [P.], seq 123:456, ack 789, win 65535, length 333
14:10:31.432 IP client > redwood: Flags [P.], seq 456:789, ack 1112, win 65535, length 0
14:10:31.433 IP redwood > client: Flags [P.], seq 1112:1445, ack 789, win 63760, length 333
```

maria_support: That pattern (long silence then receiving a PUSH with lots of data) smells like a middlebox buffering until it thinks the connection is idle then releasing. Do you have TCP keepalive or websocket-level pings enabled?

acme-sre: No app-level pings currently. We rely on the client library's default. Can you confirm Redwood's Private deployment will keep the socket active without sending data from our side for >60s?

jamal: The runtime keeps connections open; default upstream idle windows depend on infra. Suggest two mitigations to try:
- Enable periodic websocket pings from the client (every 15-25s)
- If you control the NGFW, set the idle timeout on TCP inspection to >120s or disable buffering for websocket ports

acme-sre: We'll try pings. Any server-side headers/tweaks we should check?

sre_jen: Check that your TLS terminator (if any) is passthrough or has an increased timeout. Also ensure ALB/NAT device idle timeout isn't low (e.g., AWS ALB default 60s). If using an intermediate reverse-proxy (nginx/envoy), ensure proxy_read_timeout and proxy_buffering settings allow streaming: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 300s;`

acme-sre: We do have an on-prem envoy doing TLS inspection. Hard to change config quickly. Is there a way from Redwood side to help prove it's buffering and not a TLS rehandshake?

maria_support: Yes — next steps: please run a test with wscat against the VPC endpoint while we tail the ingress on our private deployment. We'll correlate the timestamps. Also share the raw request headers (no secrets) including `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions`, `Connection`, and `Keep-Alive` headers.

acme-sre: Quick repro steps we used: `wscat -c wss://private.redwood.acme/v1/stream -n` then send a small payload and wait. Observed silence -> burst. We'll run tcpdump + wscat and upload logs.

support-bot: Ticket #65432 created and linked to this thread. SLA: P2.

jamal: If logs confirm buffering, long-term fix options: 1) recommend customers enable websocket pings; 2) add optional server-side heartbeat frames from Redwood runtime for VPC deployments behind known middleboxes (we can track as eng feature request); 3) document common firewall settings (IDS idle timeout, disable application buffering for ws).

acme-sre: We ran the ping test: with a 20s websocket ping the stream is steady. Confirms middlebox. We'll escalate to our infra team to change the NGFW idle timeout.

maria_support: Great — please keep the thread updated. We'll log the repro and add a KB entry: "Private VPC: streaming stalls due to middlebox buffering — enable client pings or increase idle timeouts."

acme-sre: Thanks all. One last ask: can you share a recommended minimal ping payload and frequency that won't interfere with rate/cost billing?

jamal: Use a 1-byte ping every 15-30s. On Redwood usage we've been conservative: pings are negligible since billing is per-token/response bytes; still, keep it small. We'll add a short FAQ item. :thumbsup:

maria_support: Marking for follow-up with eng-runtime to discuss optional server heartbeats for private deployments. cc @sre_jen @jamal

sre_jen: Noted. I'll open an internal task and link here.

acme-sre: Ok will close on our side once NGFW is adjusted. Thanks!
